component.name: granite-4.1-30b-base
component.description: IBM Granite 4.1 30B Base is a dense, decoder-only transformer language model with 30 billion parameters. Trained from scratch on approximately 15 trillion tokens using a five-phase pre-training pipeline incorporating web, code, math, multilingual, and domain-specific data. The base model serves as the foundation for the granite-4.1-30b instruct variant and is suited for fine-tuning, RAG, coding, complex reasoning, and enterprise AI workflows.

text.content: IBM Granite 4.1 30B Base model release. Structured dataset metadata used for pre- and post-training IBM Granite 4.1 base and instruct models is being released as part of IBM's effort to provide the community with highly transparent open-source model development. Machine-readable disclosure JSONs covering architecture, dataset catalogues, provenance flags, and synthetic-data indicators are published at https://github.com/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-language-models/tree/main/disclosures.

users: Enterprise software developers building AI-powered applications
AI application builders and LLM agent developers
Data scientists and ML engineers fine-tuning foundation models for domain-specific tasks
Researchers studying large-scale language model behaviour and pre-training dynamics
DevOps and platform engineers integrating models into CI/CD pipelines and RAG systems
Enterprise security analysts performing threat analysis and log summarization
useCases: Fine-tuning foundation for domain-specific enterprise AI assistants requiring the full 30B parameter capacity for complex multi-step reasoning tasks.
Serving as the backbone for agentic tool-calling workflows where the model must navigate multi-step instructions, call external APIs via JSON function schema, and synthesize results.
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines requiring deep long-document comprehension, leveraging the 128K-validated context window to ingest and reason over large corpora.
Code completion, debugging, and FIM (Fill-in-the-Middle) tasks across multiple programming languages, supported by the model's extensive code pre-training data.

Multilingual business applications requiring high-quality text generation in the 12 supported languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Arabic, Czech, Italian, Korean, Dutch, Chinese).
Complex mathematical and scientific reasoning (STEM), benefiting from extensive pre-training on math-focused datasets including NuminaMath, OpenMathReasoning, and MegaMath.
Text-to-SQL generation and structured JSON output tasks, leveraging Spider 1.0 and json-mode-reasoning post-training data.
Long-context summarization of government reports, legal documents, and financial filings, enabled by GovReport-QS and LoC-PD-Books pre-training exposure.
technicalLimitations: Context window validated to 128K tokens in standard deployment. The 512K long-context extension (Phase 5 training) may exhibit degraded coherence at extreme lengths without careful RoPE scaling configuration.
Performance degrades for languages outside the 12 explicitly supported languages. Queries in unsupported languages may produce lower-quality, inconsistent, or hallucinated responses.

As a base (non-instruct) model, granite-4.1-30b-base does not include safety-alignment fine-tuning. It is not intended for direct deployment in user-facing applications without additional post-training (SFT/RLHF).
Potential for hallucination: the model can generate factually incorrect or fabricated content, particularly for niche domains, recent events, or claims requiring precise numerical reasoning.
Reasoning gaps on novel out-of-distribution problems: despite extensive math/reasoning pre-training, complex multi-hop or adversarial reasoning may produce errors or repetition loops.
FP8 quantized variants are available only for the instruct variant. Base model inference requires BF16 at minimum, demanding substantial GPU memory for 30B parameters.

Performance varies by task domain: benchmarks represent aggregate evaluations; real-world accuracy in highly specialized fields (e.g., niche legal systems, rare programming languages) may be lower than reported scores.
performanceTradeoffs: Model size vs. inference cost: the 30B model delivers the highest reasoning accuracy in the Granite 4.1 family but requires significantly more GPU memory and compute than the 3B or 8B variants. IBM recommends 3B for edge/constrained environments, 8B for general-purpose enterprise deployment, and 30B for complex multi-step reasoning.

Long-context quality vs. context length: while the model supports up to 512K tokens via staged long-context training, production performance is validated to 128K. Using context lengths beyond 128K may reduce answer quality and increase latency without guaranteed accuracy gains.

Base vs. instruct variant: the base model offers maximum flexibility for downstream fine-tuning but lacks the safety alignment, tool-calling formatting, and instruction-following polish of the instruct variant. Deployers must account for this in their risk assessment.

BF16 precision vs. quantized inference: the base model runs in BF16 by default, offering full precision at the cost of memory. FP8 quantization (available for the instruct variant) reduces memory ~50% with minimal accuracy loss but requires FP8-capable hardware.

Breadth vs. depth of pre-training data: the five-phase pipeline allocates compute across web, code, math, multilingual, and long-context objectives. This breadth makes the model competitive across all domains but may not surpass single-domain specialist models in highly niche areas.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Training data bias and representational harm
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: IBM curated pre-training data under governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) evaluation procedures and IBM's standard data clearance and document quality review. Dataset provenance and synthetic-data flags are disclosed in machine-readable format. The HackerOne bug bounty program (up to $100K) supports ongoing adversarial red-teaming. See: https://www.ibm.com/new/announcements/ibm-granite-4-0-hyper-efficient-high-performance-hybrid-models

ethicalConsiderations.name: Hallucination and misinformation risk
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Use the granite-4.1-30b instruct variant within RAG pipelines that ground responses in verified external documents. Implement output validation layers and instruct the model to cite sources or acknowledge uncertainty. The IBM AI Risk Atlas provides a taxonomy of hallucination risk categories: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonx/saas?topic=ai-risk-atlas

ethicalConsiderations.name: Intellectual property and third-party content
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: IBM provides uncapped indemnity for third-party IP claims on content generated by Granite models when used on IBM watsonx.ai. Dataset provenance and licensing are disclosed in the machine-readable disclosure JSONs. Apache-2.0 license governs model weights.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Unsafe content generation (base model deployment risk)
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: The base model lacks safety alignment. Deployers must apply supervised fine-tuning and/or RLHF with safety-focused datasets before user-facing deployment. IBM Granite Guardian (granite-guardian-4.1-8b) is available as a companion guardrail model: https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-guardian-4.1-8b

ethicalConsiderations.name: Privacy and PII leakage risk
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: IBM's data curation pipeline applied document quality and privacy review procedures. For deployment, apply regex-based PII scrubbing to outputs and consider self-hosted deployment to prevent sensitive data from leaving the organization's security perimeter.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Environmental impact of large-scale inference
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Use FP8 quantization (instruct variant) and efficient inference engines such as vLLM with continuous batching and PagedAttention to reduce per-token FLOPs and energy consumption. The IBM Granite 4.0 architecture achieved >70% RAM reduction for long-context/concurrent workloads vs. transformer-only predecessors.

fairnessAssessments.groupAtRisk: Speakers of languages outside the 12 explicitly supported languages
fairnessAssessments.harms: Quality-of-Service harm: users querying the model in unsupported languages may receive oversimplified, factually incorrect, or hallucinated responses compared to queries in English or other well-represented training languages.
fairnessAssessments.mitigationStrategy: Restrict deployment to supported languages where quality has been validated. For multilingual extensions, apply supervised fine-tuning on high-quality parallel corpora for the target language. Clearly document supported languages in downstream application UX.

fairnessAssessments.groupAtRisk: Groups subject to societal biases present in large-scale web corpora (race, gender, religion, disability, geographic region)
fairnessAssessments.harms: The model may reflect and amplify stereotypes or representational harms present in the ~15 trillion-token pre-training corpus, which spans web, code, books, and multilingual sources.
fairnessAssessments.mitigationStrategy: IBM conducted GRC evaluations and data clearance procedures during curation. Post-training safety data (Internal Safety Data category) was used in the instruct fine-tuning pipeline. Red-teaming via HackerOne bug bounty provides ongoing adversarial evaluation. Reference the IBM AI Risk Atlas: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonx/saas?topic=ai-risk-atlas

fairnessAssessments.groupAtRisk: Users in regulated industries (finance, legal, healthcare) relying on model output for high-stakes decisions
fairnessAssessments.harms: Hallucinated or incorrect information in high-stakes domains can cause direct harm to individuals or organizations. The base model's lack of safety fine-tuning heightens this risk.
fairnessAssessments.mitigationStrategy: Granite 4.1 base is not intended for direct production deployment in regulated, high-stakes settings without additional alignment fine-tuning. Use RAG to ground responses in verified documents and implement human-in-the-loop review workflows for any consequential decisions.

properties.name: cdx:ai-ml:energy:disclosure
properties.value: No specific per-model CO2 or energy-cost figures are published in the Granite 4.1 materials. The IBM Granite 4.0 announcement documents inference efficiency improvements (>70% RAM reduction for long-context/concurrent workloads vs. transformer-only models) as a proxy for compute efficiency impact. Training infrastructure details are described in the HuggingFace Technical Blog: https://huggingface.co/blog/ibm-granite/granite-4-1

properties.name: ibm:model:disclaimer
properties.value: Structured dataset metadata used for pre- and post-training IBM Granite 4.1 base and instruct models is being released as part of IBM's effort to provide the community with highly transparent open-source model development. In this spirit, we are releasing metadata related to datasets directly ingested during training and metadata for datasets used to source seed data for IBM's synthetic data pipelines. This structured disclosure is provided in machine-readable JSON format as a governance artifact to inform risk-based controls for downstream model use.

workflows.name: Five-phase pre-training pipeline
workflows.description: Granite 4.1 30B was trained from scratch using a five-phase pre-training pipeline: phases 1–2 general pre-training on web/code/math/multilingual data; phase 3 Long CoT reasoning data injection; phase 4 PRISM-guided mid-training data retention; phase 5 staged long-context extension to 512K tokens via RoPE scaling (LoC-PD-Books as sole books source). See metadata.component.externalReferences for supporting references (HuggingFace Technical Blog, PRISM arXiv:2603.17074).

workflows.name: Post-training pipeline (instruct variant)
workflows.description: The granite-4.1-30b instruct variant was produced via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with LLM-as-Judge quality filtering, followed by a multi-stage RL pipeline using on-policy GRPO with the DAPO loss across math, code, instruction-following, function-calling, and multi-domain RL tracks. See metadata.component.externalReferences for supporting references (DAPO arXiv:2503.14476, GRPO arXiv:2402.03300, ToolRM arXiv:2509.11963).
